work.title: The Life of Timon of Athens
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. The same. The senate house

content.text: Enter three Senators at one door, Alcibiades meeting them, with Attendants.

lines.text: My lord, you have my voice to 't. The fault's
lines.plainText: My lord you have my voice to 't The fault's

lines.text: Bloody. 'Tis necessary he should die.
lines.plainText: Bloody 'Tis necessary he should die

lines.text: Nothing emboldens sin so much as mercy.
lines.plainText: Nothing emboldens sin so much as mercy

lines.text: Most true, the law shall bruise 'em.
lines.plainText: Most true the law shall bruise 'em

lines.text: Honour, health, and compassion to the senate!
lines.plainText: Honour health and compassion to the senate

lines.text: Now, captain?
lines.plainText: Now captain

lines.text: I am a humble suitor to your virtues,
lines.plainText: I am a humble suitor to your virtues

lines.text: For pity is the virtue of the law,
lines.plainText: For pity is the virtue of the law

lines.text: And none but tyrants use it cruelly.
lines.plainText: And none but tyrants use it cruelly

lines.text: It pleases time and fortune to lie heavy
lines.plainText: It pleases time and fortune to lie heavy

lines.text: Upon a friend of mine, who in hot blood
lines.plainText: Upon a friend of mine who in hot blood

lines.text: Hath stepped into the law, which is past depth
lines.plainText: Hath stepped into the law which is past depth

lines.text: To those that without heed do plunge into't.
lines.plainText: To those that without heed do plunge into't

lines.text: He is a man, setting his fate aside,
lines.plainText: He is a man setting his fate aside

lines.text: Of comely virtues,
lines.plainText: Of comely virtues

lines.text: Nor did he soil the fact with cowardice—
lines.plainText: Nor did he soil the fact with cowardice

lines.text: An honour in him which buys out his fault—
lines.plainText: An honour in him which buys out his fault

lines.text: But with a noble fury and fair spirit,
lines.plainText: But with a noble fury and fair spirit

lines.text: Seeing his reputation touched to death,
lines.plainText: Seeing his reputation touched to death

lines.text: He did oppose his foe;
lines.plainText: He did oppose his foe

lines.text: And with such sober and unnoted passion
lines.plainText: And with such sober and unnoted passion

lines.text: He did behave his anger, ere 'twas spent,
lines.plainText: He did behave his anger ere 'twas spent

lines.text: As if he had but proved an argument.
lines.plainText: As if he had but proved an argument

lines.text: You undergo too strict a paradox,
lines.plainText: You undergo too strict a paradox

lines.text: Striving to make an ugly deed look fair.
lines.plainText: Striving to make an ugly deed look fair

lines.text: Your words have took such pains as if they laboured
lines.plainText: Your words have took such pains as if they laboured

lines.text: To bring manslaughter into form and set quarrelling
lines.plainText: To bring manslaughter into form and set quarrelling

lines.text: Upon the head of valour, which indeed
lines.plainText: Upon the head of valour which indeed

lines.text: Is valour misbegot and came into the world
lines.plainText: Is valour misbegot and came into the world

lines.text: When sects and factions were newly born.
lines.plainText: When sects and factions were newly born

lines.text: He's truly valiant that can wisely suffer
lines.plainText: He's truly valiant that can wisely suffer

lines.text: The worst that man can breathe, and make his wrongs
lines.plainText: The worst that man can breathe and make his wrongs

lines.text: His outsides to wear them like his raiment, carelessly,
lines.plainText: His outsides to wear them like his raiment carelessly

lines.text: And ne'er prefer his injuries to his heart,
lines.plainText: And ne'er prefer his injuries to his heart

lines.text: To bring it into danger.
lines.plainText: To bring it into danger

lines.text: If wrongs be evils and enforce us kill,
lines.plainText: If wrongs be evils and enforce us kill

lines.text: What folly 'tis to hazard life for ill!
lines.plainText: What folly 'tis to hazard life for ill

lines.text: My lord—
lines.plainText: My lord

lines.text: You cannot make gross sins look clear.
lines.plainText: You cannot make gross sins look clear

lines.text: To revenge is no valour, but to bear.
lines.plainText: To revenge is no valour but to bear

lines.text: My lords, then, under favour, pardon me
lines.plainText: My lords then under favour pardon me

lines.text: If I speak like a captain.
lines.plainText: If I speak like a captain

lines.text: Why do fond men expose themselves to battle
lines.plainText: Why do fond men expose themselves to battle

lines.text: And not endure all threats? Sleep upon't,
lines.plainText: And not endure all threats Sleep upon't

lines.text: And let the foes quietly cut their throats
lines.plainText: And let the foes quietly cut their throats

lines.text: Without repugnancy? If there be
lines.plainText: Without repugnancy If there be

lines.text: Such valour in the bearing, what make we
lines.plainText: Such valour in the bearing what make we

lines.text: Abroad? Why, then, women are more valiant
lines.plainText: Abroad Why then women are more valiant

lines.text: That stay at home, if bearing carry it,
lines.plainText: That stay at home if bearing carry it

lines.text: And the ass more captain than the lion, the felon
lines.plainText: And the ass more captain than the lion the felon

lines.text: Loaden with irons wiser than the judge,
lines.plainText: Loaden with irons wiser than the judge

lines.text: If wisdom be in suffering. O my lords,
lines.plainText: If wisdom be in suffering O my lords

lines.text: As you are great, be pitifully good.
lines.plainText: As you are great be pitifully good

lines.text: Who cannot condemn rashness in cold blood?
lines.plainText: Who cannot condemn rashness in cold blood

lines.text: To kill, I grant, is sin's extremest gust,
lines.plainText: To kill I grant is sin's extremest gust

lines.text: But in defence, by mercy, 'tis most just.
lines.plainText: But in defence by mercy 'tis most just

lines.text: To be in anger is impiety,
lines.plainText: To be in anger is impiety

lines.text: But who is man that is not angry?
lines.plainText: But who is man that is not angry

lines.text: Weigh but the crime with this.
lines.plainText: Weigh but the crime with this

lines.text: You breathe in vain.
lines.plainText: You breathe in vain

lines.text: In vain? His service done
lines.plainText: In vain His service done

lines.text: At Lacedaemon and Byzantium
lines.plainText: At Lacedaemon and Byzantium

lines.text: Were a sufficient briber for his life.
lines.plainText: Were a sufficient briber for his life

lines.text: What's that?
lines.plainText: What's that

lines.text: Why, I say, my lords, has done fair service
lines.plainText: Why I say my lords has done fair service

lines.text: And slain in fight many of your enemies.
lines.plainText: And slain in fight many of your enemies

lines.text: How full of valour did he bear himself
lines.plainText: How full of valour did he bear himself

lines.text: In the last conflict, and made plenteous wounds!
lines.plainText: In the last conflict and made plenteous wounds

lines.text: He has made too much plenty with 'em.
lines.plainText: He has made too much plenty with 'em

lines.text: He's a sworn rioter. He has a sin
lines.plainText: He's a sworn rioter He has a sin

lines.text: That often drowns him and takes his valour prisoner.
lines.plainText: That often drowns him and takes his valour prisoner

lines.text: If there were no foes, that were enough
lines.plainText: If there were no foes that were enough

lines.text: To overcome him. In that beastly fury,
lines.plainText: To overcome him In that beastly fury

lines.text: He has been known to commit outrages
lines.plainText: He has been known to commit outrages

lines.text: And cherish factions. 'Tis inferred to us
lines.plainText: And cherish factions 'Tis inferred to us

lines.text: His days are foul and his drink dangerous.
lines.plainText: His days are foul and his drink dangerous

lines.text: He dies.
lines.plainText: He dies

lines.text: Hard fate! He might have died in war.
lines.plainText: Hard fate He might have died in war

lines.text: My lords, if not for any parts in him,
lines.plainText: My lords if not for any parts in him

lines.text: Though his right arm might purchase his own time
lines.plainText: Though his right arm might purchase his own time

lines.text: And be in debt to none, yet, more to move you,
lines.plainText: And be in debt to none yet more to move you

lines.text: Take my deserts to his and join 'em both.
lines.plainText: Take my deserts to his and join 'em both

lines.text: And, for I know your reverend ages love
lines.plainText: And for I know your reverend ages love

lines.text: Security, I'll pawn my victories, all
lines.plainText: Security I'll pawn my victories all

lines.text: My honour, to you upon his good returns.
lines.plainText: My honour to you upon his good returns

lines.text: If by this crime he owes the law his life,
lines.plainText: If by this crime he owes the law his life

lines.text: Why, let the war receive't in valiant gore,
lines.plainText: Why let the war receive't in valiant gore

lines.text: For law is strict, and war is nothing more.
lines.plainText: For law is strict and war is nothing more

lines.text: We are for law. He dies. Urge it no more,
lines.plainText: We are for law He dies Urge it no more

lines.text: On height of our displeasure. Friend or brother,
lines.plainText: On height of our displeasure Friend or brother

lines.text: He forfeits his own blood that spills another.
lines.plainText: He forfeits his own blood that spills another

lines.text: Must it be so? It must not be.
lines.plainText: Must it be so It must not be

lines.text: My lords, I do beseech you, know me.
lines.plainText: My lords I do beseech you know me

lines.text: How?
lines.plainText: How

lines.text: Call me to your remembrances.
lines.plainText: Call me to your remembrances

lines.text: What?
lines.plainText: What

lines.text: I cannot think but your age has forgot me,
lines.plainText: I cannot think but your age has forgot me

lines.text: It could not else be I should prove so base
lines.plainText: It could not else be I should prove so base

lines.text: To sue and be denied such common grace.
lines.plainText: To sue and be denied such common grace

lines.text: My wounds ache at you.
lines.plainText: My wounds ache at you

lines.text: Do you dare our anger?
lines.plainText: Do you dare our anger

lines.text: 'Tis in few words, but spacious in effect:
lines.plainText: 'Tis in few words but spacious in effect

lines.text: We banish thee for ever.
lines.plainText: We banish thee for ever

lines.text: Banish me?
lines.plainText: Banish me

lines.text: Banish your dotage, banish usury,
lines.plainText: Banish your dotage banish usury

lines.text: That makes the Senate ugly.
lines.plainText: That makes the Senate ugly

lines.text: If, after two days' shine, Athens contain thee,
lines.plainText: If after two days' shine Athens contain thee

lines.text: Attend our weightier judgment.
lines.plainText: Attend our weightier judgment

lines.text: And, not to swell our spirit,
lines.plainText: And not to swell our spirit

lines.text: He shall be executed presently.
lines.plainText: He shall be executed presently

lines.text: Now the gods keep you old enough, that you may live
lines.plainText: Now the gods keep you old enough that you may live

lines.text: Only in bone, that none may look on you!
lines.plainText: Only in bone that none may look on you

lines.text: I'm worse than mad. I have kept back their foes
lines.plainText: I'm worse than mad I have kept back their foes

lines.text: While they have told their money and let out
lines.plainText: While they have told their money and let out

lines.text: Their coin upon large interest, I myself
lines.plainText: Their coin upon large interest I myself

lines.text: Rich only in large hurts. All those for this?
lines.plainText: Rich only in large hurts All those for this

lines.text: Is this the balsam that the usuring senate
lines.plainText: Is this the balsam that the usuring senate

lines.text: Pours into captains' wounds? Banishment.
lines.plainText: Pours into captains' wounds Banishment

lines.text: It comes not ill. I hate not to be banished.
lines.plainText: It comes not ill I hate not to be banished

lines.text: It is a cause worthy my spleen and fury,
lines.plainText: It is a cause worthy my spleen and fury

lines.text: That I may strike at Athens. I'll cheer up
lines.plainText: That I may strike at Athens I'll cheer up

lines.text: My discontented troops and lay for hearts.
lines.plainText: My discontented troops and lay for hearts

lines.text: 'Tis honour with most lands to be at odds.
lines.plainText: 'Tis honour with most lands to be at odds

lines.text: Soldiers should brook as little wrongs as gods.
lines.plainText: Soldiers should brook as little wrongs as gods
